source_user: A multi-GPU job hangs during collective initialization. Provide a diagnosis plan. Scenario variant 121: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: record ranks and environment; verify process-group rendezvous; inspect topology and GPU visibility; run a minimal all-reduce; test interface selection and timeout; compare single-node and reduced-world runs.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions and safety: this is diagnosis, not proof of a root cause. Backend, launcher, library/driver versions, world size, placement, scheduler, container privileges, fabric, interface, topology, and blocked stage are unknown; record each as measured or estimated. Use only an authorized isolated allocation, redact endpoints and credentials, impose a finite watchdog, and clean up processes and temporary state.

Measurements: assign a run ID and capture per-rank host, global/local rank, expected and observed membership, PID, device mapping, software/configuration hashes, redacted rendezvous/store identifier, process-group and collective entry/exit timestamps, last progress, stderr/backend debug logs, GPU/NIC IDs, interface/address/route/DNS/MTU/firewall state, peer access, PCIe/NVLink topology, container device/shared-memory visibility, ulimits, and clock synchronization. Confirm every expected rank starts exactly once, uses the same rendezvous endpoint/world size, and enters collectives in the same order.

Hypothesis: the hang is caused by a rank-specific membership or rendezvous/transport mismatch, rather than a generic GPU failure. It predicts that the first missing or stalled rank will show divergent membership, endpoint, interface, route, or collective-entry evidence, and that a matched reduced-world or single-node run will complete. Falsify it if all ranks have identical membership and transport evidence, the minimal collective completes under the same configuration, or the hang persists identically after transport/interface isolation.

Controlled experiment: with fixed software, allocation, message sizes, timeout, and rank logging, randomize repeated trials across single-node, reduced-world, and full-world cases. Run a minimal init plus all-reduce and a barrier, then vary only world size and explicitly authorized interface selection; use a bounded timeout. Compare per-rank entry/exit, error, latency, timeout, checksum/correctness, and cleanup results with confidence intervals, not just successes. Check topology/GPU visibility and collective order before interpreting results.

Confounders and decisions: consider collective-order divergence, stale rendezvous state, wrong rank/device mapping, DNS/firewall/MTU/route issues, incompatible backend/library/driver, NIC/GPU topology, container limits, resource exhaustion, clock skew, and scheduler placement. Preserve logs and a redacted manifest. Stop and roll back if correctness differs, errors/timeouts rise, or cleanup is incomplete; do not change production settings without authorization. Evidence required: per-rank logs and timestamps, exact versions/config hashes, endpoint/interface evidence, topology/device maps, trial matrix/raw outcomes, and expert review. Scenario variant 121 is not platform-specific evidence. This provisional conclusion is low-to-moderate confidence and requires domain validation.
risks: Root cause remains unproven without per-rank artifacts and domain review.
Interface or timeout changes can mask rather than fix a failure.
Logs may contain sensitive endpoints or identifiers and require redaction.
evidence_required: per-rank membership, rendezvous, entry/exit timestamps, and backend logs
randomized matched trial outcomes with correctness, latency, timeout, and cleanup denominators
